title: Advanced Manufacturing
description: This course provides an understanding of industry technology and exposure to advanced manufacturing, pneumatics, electronics, mechatronics, and vacuum systems.
outcomes: Upon completion of the course, students will be able to describe elements and basic troubleshooting of circuits.
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to describe manufacturing concerns and troubleshooting procedures.
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to read and interpret diagrams for mechanical, gas, and electrical systems.
objectives: Electronics
Describe the basic electrical elements, such as power supplies, components of circuits, and basics of electrical conduction
Explain electrical safety concerns for working with electrical systems
Explain the terms, units, and qualitative properties of voltage, current, resistance, and power, as applied to DC and AC electrical circuits
Use basic measurement tools and methods for voltage, current, and resistance measurements
Identify symbols and connections for components using diagrams
Perform wiring of control circuits working from diagrams
Explain the basic operating principals of programmable logic controllers
Troubleshoot electro-mechanical systems
Understand safety techniques in an industrial environment
Chemical/Gas delivery
Understand safety practices
Understand possible chemical reactions
Mechatronics
Describe motors and how they work
Present an overview of programmable logic controllers (PLC)
Explain control systems: Open and closed loops
Identify concepts of electro-mechanical systems
Demonstrate the use of various sensors to monitor clean room processes
Troubleshoot electro-mechanical systems
Basic vacuum technology
Understand gas kinetic theory
Understand bulk behavior vs. molecular behavior
Use equations to relate gas flow and pumpdown time
Identify vacuum sealing surfaces and basic fittings
Demonstrate ability to read vacuum gauges and different types of gauges
Explain differences in type of vacuum pumps
Understand the importance of leak detection
Advanced manufacturing practices
Follow procedures and methods for using tools
Follow procedures for reporting issues
Identify steps in a procedure from diagrams
Identify contact person for various issues
Understand level of urgency needed in various situations
Communicate effectively in various clean room scenarios
content: Electrical safety concerns for people and equipment
Measurement tools and methods for voltage, current, and resistance measurements
Control systems: Open and closed loops
Gas flow and pumpdown time equations
Procedures and methods for using tools
